package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware targeting Linux servers, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects Linux servers, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: Erebus ransomware encrypts files on Linux servers, rendering data inaccessible and demanding ransom for decryption. The malware is intentionally designed to extort victims by denying access to critical data and services.

execution_context.file_location: infected Linux server (location varies, typically /tmp or /var/tmp or as a dropped binary)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: for file in $(find / -type f); do encrypt $file; done
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code recursively enumerates all files on the filesystem and encrypts each file, resulting in denial of access to all user and system data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass file encryption across the entire filesystem is a hallmark of ransomware and is never part of legitimate server operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal server processes do not encrypt all files or modify them in bulk without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or migration scripts may access many files, but do not encrypt or render them inaccessible.

execution_context.file_location: infected Linux server (ransom note dropped in root and user directories)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: echo 'Your files have been encrypted. Pay 1 BTC to the following address to recover your data.' > /root/README_FOR_DECRYPT.txt
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After encrypting files, the code writes a ransom note to prominent directories, instructing the victim to pay a ransom for decryption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping ransom notes is a direct indicator of ransomware activity and is never part of legitimate software behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not demand payment for access to user data.

attack_chain.action: Malware is executed on the Linux server, gaining access to the filesystem.
All files on the server are recursively encrypted, denying access to data.
Ransom note is written to disk, instructing the victim to pay for decryption.

behavioral_signatures: Bulk file access and modification in a short time window
Creation of ransom note files with payment instructions
Unusual process activity not matching known software
file_indicators: Unusual file extensions appended to user files
network_indicators: Outbound connections to cryptocurrency payment addresses (may be in ransom note)
Possible C2 communication if malware reports infection
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that rapidly access and modify large numbers of files, especially if file extensions change or files become unreadable. Watch for the creation of ransom note files in root or user directories. Alert on any process that writes files containing cryptocurrency payment instructions. Correlate with any unusual outbound network activity, especially to known cryptocurrency services or suspicious domains.
